images.title: A rectangle's diagonals make isosceles triangles
images.purpose: Shows rectangle ABCD whose diagonals meet at O, with ∠CAB = 30° giving the equal angle ∠ABD = 30° and 120° at O.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rectangle in the centre with both diagonals, the bottom triangle at the crossing picked out.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD in dark outline, about 1.73 times as wide as it is tall, with A bottom left, B bottom right, C top right and D top left. The diagonals AC and BD are thick dark lines crossing at O. The bottom triangle AOB is lightly filled teal (#0072B2); the half diagonals OA and OB each carry one short tick mark. A small amber (#E69F00) arc at A between AB and AC is labelled 30°, and a matching amber arc at B between BA and BD is labelled 30°. A small reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc at O inside triangle AOB is labelled 120°. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners and O sits just above the crossing. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The half diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so each small triangle is isosceles.

image_decisions.why: The one shaded isosceles triangle is the key step for every angle hunt inside a rectangle.
